title_zh: 可以走，还不等于有路走
title_en: Permission to Leave Is Not Yet a Way Forward
deck_zh: 从窑工的离职条款，到照护中的代为决定：要问的不只是这份安排对他有没有好处，还有他自己的事，最后握在谁手里。
deck_en: An advance, a training offer, or help with decisions can benefit someone. That does not settle who controls their departure, their next direction, or choices they can still make themselves.
body_zh: 在这个虚构的王国州，一位老窑工想离开青窑瓷业。他还有预支没有还清。合同写着，预支未清，离职须经公司同意。手艺是他的，下一段生活也是他的，但走之前，还得等别人点头。
不妨把公司想得更好一点：它从没拒绝过谁。每个提出离职的人都得到了同意，预支也确实帮人渡过难关。这样一来，条款就没有问题了吗？和气的答复可以改变一次经历，却没有取消“我想走，须你准许”的安排。
点头本身，也是在使用那个决定位置。问题不必等到第一次被拒才出现。但这还不足以断言退出已完全封死：若有还清款项的可用通道，也要一起看。既不能把未见拒绝说成毫无控制，也不能省掉事实，直接宣布人已无路可走。
有通知期、有程序、有代价，都不自动等于不能离开。要核的是，离开、拒绝或撤回一段持续关系的路，是否仍由本人掌握，或能转入可审查的程序；也要看他的生计能否承受。纸上写着“可以”，不一定是生活里走得动。
还要再问一步：离开之后，有没有去处可选？人可以走出厂门，却被禁止到同业工作，门外依然有人替他定方向。退得出，与选得了，是两件相互支持、不能互相代替的事；出路的多少可以不同，不该由别人先把方向封死。
这也不是把所有工作安排都叫作控制。什么时候交货，谁值哪一班，是共同工作的事项，可以由有职责的人在规定范围内安排，并受追问。一个能自己决定的人，要不要离开、往哪里去，却不能同样交给雇主作主。
利弊当然仍要算。一条约定可能保护公司的培训投入，也可能换来较高收入；另一些人却因它错过机会。只问“对谁更好”，答案常随站位改变。先看安排拿走了什么，能够让争论多一个不跟着好意与收益移动的根据，却不保证事实争议从此消失。
青窑还有另一条约定：离职后两年内，不得在州内为其他瓷器企业工作，违反要付相当于十二个月工资的钱。在故事里，一位窑工得到外部出资，谈妥补偿才脱身；两位没有这份支持的同事仍留在那里。这里的合同号与期限都是设例，不是某地现行法律。
若补偿足够多，条款是否就变成好安排？若本人签了字呢？这一系列的回答仍是不允许用违约金、禁令或强制执行，替人禁止离开后的去向。补偿改变代价，签字说明一种同意，二者都没有把被拿走的选择还回来。这是明确的规范立场，不是法律现状的概括。
反对者有一个不能轻轻带过的理由。没有本钱的人，可能正想用未来的承诺，换今天的培训和岗位。限制选项，有时确实使承诺更可信，也可能对承诺者有利。若一概不许这种禁止，有些双方原本愿意做的交易，可能就做不成了。
这份代价要承认，不能用“其实大家都会更好”抹掉。这里选择守住的是：一个人可以承担有代价的承诺，却不能把自己离开以后往哪里去交由别人禁止。不同意这一条的人，争的是底线本身，不只是还没算清哪一种经济效果。
但有另一种安排，可以分开读：不去竞争，就额外领一笔钱；去竞争，只停止这一笔新增给付。必须同时核三件事：后果只是停止给付，那笔钱确实在已有之外，而本人在现实中也拒绝得起。满足这些条件，不在这里直接判为侵犯；具体规则仍可选择不允许。
“去竞争就赔一万”与“不去就多领一万”，在账面上的差额可以相同。可前一种碰的是他已经有的东西，后一种可能是尚未取得的新增机会。不能只算两条路相差多少钱，省掉钱本来属于谁，以及怎样丧失的问题。
归属要独立查，不能由正在受审的那份条款自己命名。做完工作应得的工资、已经归属的股权，不因改称奖励就变成额外。先核什么已经挣得，再看单是离职本来会失去什么，这项约定又多加了什么后果。分不清的，仍要具体认定。
先把说定的工资压低，再把同一块钱改名为不竞争补贴，也不能洗成新增。更深的依赖也要合看：若拒绝就活不下去，纵使后果表面上只是不再给，也不能认定他真有选择。这里不保证每一种禁令，都找得到功能完全相同的温和替代。
企业确有需要保护的东西。正当的配方与保密信息可以保护，但一般技能、客户本人和客户的选择，不是企业的财产。培训投入可以另谈服务与退出条件；保密、服务期这些名字，也不能替实际范围证明清白。
为保护第三人权利或公共审查而设的离任约束，则需要另说根据：限制哪一种行为，保护谁，为什么更少的限制不够，范围多大。它不是只因也限制了去处，就与雇主排除竞争的条款混为一谈；超出保护所需的部分，仍须受问。
到这里，另一个场景会拦住过于快的结论。虚构的南窗养老院里，有护理员替老人安排服药、起居与夜间外出。这些也涉及本人。难道凡是代为决定，都是同一种越界吗？必须先把那位具体的老人重新放回来。
住在失智护理区，不证明他在每件事上都不能决定。不同意护理员的选择，也不证明没有能力。若在某件事上确实不能自行决定，这里的讨论才允许有限的代为处理；能决定的那些事，仍由本人决定，不因入住而整体交出。
至少要有具体根据、由制度划定而非照护方自定的范围，以及能追问、能纠正的通道。能力是否恢复、原先判断是否还成立，要能重看。没有固定期限，不自动使照护不当；同样，也不取消事前约束、日常监督与事后回应。三项条件必要，却不是一张自动正当的许可证。
适用于英格兰与威尔士的2005年《心智能力法》的原则，先推定有能力，要求尽力提供帮助，不因选择不明智就认定无能力，同时提出最佳利益与更少限制的要求。这是一种法律文本的安排，不是诊断方法，也不是用来替当前个案作决定的说明书。
这里还存在真正的分歧。联合国残疾人权利委员会2014年第一号一般性意见，反对依心智能力评估剥夺法律能力，要求以辅助决定取代替代决定。因而，它并不赞成刚才那种“按事项认定不能，再容许代为处理”的原则。不能把双方写成已经对齐。
这一系列仍承担有限代为处理的可能，但不以别人眼中的“为你好”替本人选一条人生。若尽力后难以辨认意愿，应尽量依据对其意愿与偏好的最佳解释；仍辨不出的，先保护基本生活与尊严，不替他决定如何追求幸福。这一建议在方向上接近委员会，却没有消除根本分歧。
有些处境仍然难办，甚至暂时无答案。承认原则没有写尽，不是推导出谁都可以接手的许可；也不能把“我们有程序”当作允许替一位能自行决定的人作主。规章本身仍须有根据，使用它的人仍要说明限度。
这条路也不以离职一项取代所有保护。即使随时能走，工作中仍可能有不当干预，仍需要对管理决定提出异议的实际办法。退出与发声不足以互相代替，这一点并非新发现；工作场所民主、工会或其他复核安排，如何组合，还要继续做具体工作。
回到厂门口。好的支持，可以让那位窑工有饭吃、学新手艺、试另一条路，而不把帮助换成替他决定的权力。真正值得留下的关系，不该主要靠走不了维持；帮助也不该因为做过好事，就取得接管余下人生的资格。
body_en: In the fictional Kingdom State, an experienced kiln worker wants to leave Bluekiln Porcelain Works. An advance remains unpaid. His contract says departure requires the company's consent until it is cleared. The craft is his, and the next part of his life is his. For now, however, he must wait for someone else to agree.

Make the employer kinder. It has never refused anyone, and its advances genuinely help workers through difficult periods. Does that remove the problem? A generous answer changes an experience without removing the arrangement: my departure remains something for you to authorize. The distinction concerns the relationship, not a prediction of bad intentions.

Approval itself exercises that position; we need not wait for the first refusal. But the clause alone does not prove that every exit is blocked. An available repayment route matters too. Neither absence of refusal nor a troubling clause can substitute for examining what paths actually remain and whether people can use them.

Notice periods, procedures, costs, and deadlines do not automatically eliminate exit. Ask whether leaving, refusing, or withdrawing from an ongoing relationship remains in the person's hands, or can enter a reviewable procedure. Livelihood matters as well. A paper permission is not necessarily a journey someone can afford to make.

Then ask what follows departure. Someone may walk out of the factory while being prohibited from working in their trade elsewhere. The exit opens onto a direction already closed by another party. Being able to leave and having options afterward support each other without being identical. Unequal numbers of opportunities are not the same as an externally prohibited direction.

This does not turn every work instruction into improper control. Delivery schedules and shifts concern joint activity. Someone with defined responsibilities can arrange them within an answerable scope. Whether a person capable of deciding will leave, and where they will go afterward, cannot simply become another managerial assignment.

Benefits still count. A restriction might protect training investment or help secure higher pay while costing someone else an opportunity. Asking only who benefits can move the conclusion with the beneficiary. Examining what an arrangement removes supplies another criterion. It does not magically resolve factual disagreements about costs, options, or actual dependence.

Bluekiln's fictional contract has another clause: no work for competing porcelain firms in the state for two years, backed by a payment equivalent to twelve months' wages. One worker escapes after outside funding helps negotiate a release; two without it remain. These provisions belong to an invented case, not a statement of any jurisdiction's current law.

Would sufficient compensation make the prohibition acceptable? Would a signature? This series says no to contractual penalties, injunctions, or enforcement prohibiting a person's post-exit direction. Compensation changes cost; consent records agreement. Neither restores the prohibited option. That is an explicit normative commitment, not a summary of what courts currently enforce.

A serious objection must remain visible. A worker without capital may want to pledge a future restriction in exchange for training and a job today. Limiting options can sometimes make a commitment credible and benefit its maker. Refusing that device may prevent some transactions that both sides would otherwise choose.

That cost should not be erased by promising that everyone will really be better off. The boundary defended here is that costly commitments cannot hand someone else authority to prohibit a person's post-exit direction. Disagreement concerns the boundary itself, not merely a failure to calculate the most advantageous bargain.

A different arrangement deserves separate examination: do not compete and receive an additional payment; compete and that new payment stops. Three conditions must hold together. The consequence is only cessation of payment, it is genuinely additional to what is already the person's, and declining it is practically affordable. This argument does not categorically condemn that arrangement, though specific rules may still prohibit it.

Pay a penalty for competing and receive a bonus for not competing can produce the same numerical difference between choices. Their structure can nevertheless differ. The former takes something already held; the latter may offer a genuinely new opportunity. Arithmetic alone omits ownership and the mechanism by which a person loses something.

Ownership must be examined independently of the disputed clause's labels. Earned wages or vested equity do not become extras when renamed rewards. Establish what has been earned, then compare what departure alone would lose with consequences added by the condition. Uncertain entitlements require determination, not a convenient assumption that every disputed sum is new.

Cutting agreed wages and relabeling the same amount as a noncompetition supplement cannot perform that transformation. Other constraints matter too: if refusal means inability to subsist, mere cessation of payment does not establish a real choice. Nor is there a guarantee that every prohibited arrangement has a gentler substitute with exactly the same economic function.

Employers have legitimate interests to protect. Properly confidential formulas and information can be protected; general skills, customers themselves, and customers' choices are not corporate possessions. Training can have separately justified service and exit arrangements. Calling a restriction confidentiality or a service period does not establish that its actual scope leaves future directions open.

Restrictions protecting others' rights or public scrutiny need their own account: which conduct is limited, whose protection requires it, why a lesser restriction is insufficient, and how wide it extends. A cooling-off arrangement is not automatically identical to excluding competition simply because both affect destinations. Excess beyond its protective justification remains challengeable.

Another scene complicates any hurried conclusion. In fictional Southwindow Care Homes, staff arrange medication, waking times, and nighttime outings for residents. These also concern a person's life. Is every decision made on another's behalf the same wrong? First put the particular resident, rather than an institutional category, back into the question.

Living in a dementia unit does not establish inability to make every decision. Disagreeing with a caregiver does not establish it either. Only where a person genuinely cannot decide a particular matter does this argument allow limited handling on their behalf. Matters they can decide remain theirs; admission does not transfer a whole life.

At minimum, this requires specific grounds, scope defined through institutional rules rather than unilaterally by the provider, and effective questioning and correction. Changed ability requires reconsideration. Indefinite care is not automatically improper, but it still needs advance constraints, ongoing supervision, and responses afterward. These are necessary conditions, not a sufficient certificate of justification.

The principles of England and Wales's Mental Capacity Act 2005 presume capacity, require practicable assistance, and distinguish an unwise choice from inability, alongside best-interests and less-restrictive requirements. This is a legal arrangement offered for comparison, not a diagnostic test or instructions for deciding a present care case.

A genuine disagreement remains. The UN disability-rights committee's 2014 General Comment No.1 rejects denial of legal capacity through mental-capacity assessment and calls for supported rather than substitute decision-making. It does not endorse the preceding permission to identify inability in a particular matter and then allow another person to decide. The positions must not be made artificially equivalent.

This series still accepts a limited possibility of acting on another's behalf, without replacing their direction with someone else's preferred good. After substantial efforts, uncertain wishes call for the best interpretation of their will and preferences. Where those cannot be discerned, protect basic life and dignity rather than assign a pursuit of happiness. This approaches part of the committee's guidance without resolving the fundamental disagreement.

Some cases remain difficult or unanswered. Admitting that principles do not cover everything does not grant a general license to take over. Having procedures cannot justify deciding for someone who can decide the matter themselves. Rules need grounds of their own; those applying them must explain their reach and limits.

Exit is not the whole protection either. Improper interference at work can coexist with the ability to leave. People still need effective ways to challenge managerial decisions. This is not a novel observation. Workplace democracy, unions, and other review arrangements offer forms whose particular combination requires further institutional work.

Return to the factory door. Support can feed the worker, develop a skill, or help him try another route without purchasing authority over the next decision. A relationship worth remaining in should not depend primarily on making departure impossible. Help already given cannot become a title to the rest of someone's life.

body_hant: 在這個虛構的王國州，一位老窯工想離開青窯瓷業。他還有預支沒有還清。合同寫著，預支未清，離職須經公司同意。手藝是他的，下一段生活也是他的，但走之前，還得等別人點頭。
不妨把公司想得更好一點：它從沒拒絕過誰。每個提出離職的人都得到了同意，預支也確實幫人渡過難關。這樣一來，條款就沒有問題了嗎？和氣的答覆可以改變一次經歷，卻沒有取消「我想走，須你准許」的安排。
點頭本身，也是在使用那個決定位置。問題不必等到第一次被拒才出現。但這還不足以斷言退出已完全封死：若有還清款項的可用通道，也要一起看。既不能把未見拒絕說成毫無控制，也不能省掉事實，直接宣佈人已無路可走。
有通知期、有程序、有代價，都不自動等於不能離開。要核的是，離開、拒絕或撤回一段持續關係的路，是否仍由本人掌握，或能轉入可審查的程序；也要看他的生計能否承受。紙上寫著「可以」，不一定是生活裡走得動。
還要再問一步：離開之後，有沒有去處可選？人可以走出廠門，卻被禁止到同業工作，門外依然有人替他定方向。退得出，與選得了，是兩件相互支持、不能互相代替的事；出路的多少可以不同，不該由別人先把方向封死。
這也不是把所有工作安排都叫作控制。什麼時候交貨，誰值哪一班，是共同工作的事項，可以由有職責的人在規定範圍內安排，並受追問。一個能自己決定的人，要不要離開、往哪裡去，卻不能同樣交給雇主作主。
利弊當然仍要算。一條約定可能保護公司的培訓投入，也可能換來較高收入；另一些人卻因它錯過機會。只問「對誰更好」，答案常隨站位改變。先看安排拿走了什麼，能夠讓爭論多一個不跟著好意與收益移動的根據，卻不保證事實爭議從此消失。
青窯還有另一條約定：離職後兩年內，不得在州內為其他瓷器企業工作，違反要付相當於十二個月工資的錢。在故事裡，一位窯工得到外部出資，談妥補償才脫身；兩位沒有這份支持的同事仍留在那裡。這裡的合同號與期限都是設例，不是某地現行法律。
若補償足夠多，條款是否就變成好安排？若本人簽了字呢？這一系列的回答仍是不允許用違約金、禁令或強制執行，替人禁止離開後的去向。補償改變代價，簽字說明一種同意，二者都沒有把被拿走的選擇還回來。這是明確的規範立場，不是法律現狀的概括。
反對者有一個不能輕輕帶過的理由。沒有本錢的人，可能正想用未來的承諾，換今天的培訓和崗位。限制選項，有時確實使承諾更可信，也可能對承諾者有利。若一概不許這種禁止，有些雙方原本願意做的交易，可能就做不成了。
這份代價要承認，不能用「其實大家都會更好」抹掉。這裡選擇守住的是：一個人可以承擔有代價的承諾，卻不能把自己離開以後往哪裡去交由別人禁止。不同意這一條的人，爭的是底線本身，不只是還沒算清哪一種經濟效果。
但有另一種安排，可以分開讀：不去競爭，就額外領一筆錢；去競爭，只停止這一筆新增給付。必須同時核三件事：後果只是停止給付，那筆錢確實在已有之外，而本人在現實中也拒絕得起。滿足這些條件，不在這裡直接判為侵犯；具體規則仍可選擇不允許。
「去競爭就賠一萬」與「不去就多領一萬」，在帳面上的差額可以相同。可前一種碰的是他已經有的東西，後一種可能是尚未取得的新增機會。不能只算兩條路相差多少錢，省掉錢本來屬於誰，以及怎樣喪失的問題。
歸屬要獨立查，不能由正在受審的那份條款自己命名。做完工作應得的工資、已經歸屬的股權，不因改稱獎勵就變成額外。先核什麼已經掙得，再看單是離職本來會失去什麼，這項約定又多加了什麼後果。分不清的，仍要具體認定。
先把說定的工資壓低，再把同一塊錢改名為不競爭補貼，也不能洗成新增。更深的依賴也要合看：若拒絕就活不下去，縱使後果表面上只是不再給，也不能認定他真有選擇。這裡不保證每一種禁令，都找得到功能完全相同的溫和替代。
企業確有需要保護的東西。正當的配方與保密資訊可以保護，但一般技能、客戶本人和客戶的選擇，不是企業的財產。培訓投入可以另談服務與退出條件；保密、服務期這些名字，也不能替實際範圍證明清白。
為保護第三人權利或公共審查而設的離任約束，則需要另說根據：限制哪一種行為，保護誰，為什麼更少的限制不夠，範圍多大。它不是只因也限制了去處，就與雇主排除競爭的條款混為一談；超出保護所需的部分，仍須受問。
到這裡，另一個場景會攔住過於快的結論。虛構的南窗養老院裡，有護理員替老人安排服藥、起居與夜間外出。這些也涉及本人。難道凡是代為決定，都是同一種越界嗎？必須先把那位具體的老人重新放回來。
住在失智護理區，不證明他在每件事上都不能決定。不同意護理員的選擇，也不證明沒有能力。若在某件事上確實不能自行決定，這裡的討論才允許有限的代為處理；能決定的那些事，仍由本人決定，不因入住而整體交出。
至少要有具體根據、由制度劃定而非照護方自定的範圍，以及能追問、能糾正的通道。能力是否恢復、原先判斷是否還成立，要能重看。沒有固定期限，不自動使照護不當；同樣，也不取消事前約束、日常監督與事後回應。三項條件必要，卻不是一張自動正當的許可證。
適用於英格蘭與威爾士的2005年《心智能力法》的原則，先推定有能力，要求盡力提供幫助，不因選擇不明智就認定無能力，同時提出最佳利益與更少限制的要求。這是一種法律文本的安排，不是診斷方法，也不是用來替當前個案作決定的說明書。
這裡還存在真正的分歧。聯合國殘疾人權利委員會2014年第一號一般性意見，反對依心智能力評估剝奪法律能力，要求以輔助決定取代替代決定。因而，它並不贊成剛才那種「按事項認定不能，再容許代為處理」的原則。不能把雙方寫成已經對齊。
這一系列仍承擔有限代為處理的可能，但不以別人眼中的「為你好」替本人選一條人生。若盡力後難以辨認意願，應盡量依據對其意願與偏好的最佳解釋；仍辨不出的，先保護基本生活與尊嚴，不替他決定如何追求幸福。這一建議在方向上接近委員會，卻沒有消除根本分歧。
有些處境仍然難辦，甚至暫時無答案。承認原則沒有寫盡，不是推導出誰都可以接手的許可；也不能把「我們有程序」當作允許替一位能自行決定的人作主。規章本身仍須有根據，使用它的人仍要說明限度。
這條路也不以離職一項取代所有保護。即使隨時能走，工作中仍可能有不當干預，仍需要對管理決定提出異議的實際辦法。退出與發聲不足以互相代替，這一點並非新發現；工作場所民主、工會或其他複核安排，如何組合，還要繼續做具體工作。
回到廠門口。好的支持，可以讓那位窯工有飯吃、學新手藝、試另一條路，而不把幫助換成替他決定的權力。真正值得留下的關係，不該主要靠走不了維持；幫助也不該因為做過好事，就取得接管餘下人生的資格。
